strengths: Novel analysis framework with trajectory-level and step-level granularity providing fresh perspective beyond Pass@k metrics
Comprehensive empirical study across multiple model sizes (1.5B-14B), architectures (Qwen, DeepSeek-R1, Llama), and datasets (AIME24/25, AMC23)
Multiple complementary analysis techniques (trajectory clustering, reasoning graphs, exponential decay rates, 8 topology metrics, graphlet analysis) strengthen conclusions
Well-written with clear presentation and informative visualizations that effectively communicate complex analyses
Extensive implementation details and appendices support reproducibility
weaknesses: Core findings are largely confirmatory of existing Pass@k analysis (Yue et al. 2025) rather than providing novel understanding; the 'squeeze/expand' observation aligns with known phenomena
Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper shows what happens (decay rate changes, topology shifts) but not why these properties emerge or why they matter for performance

Critical gap unresolved: similar local structures (graphlets) across RL/SFT/SFT+RL models yet substantially different performance; paper acknowledges 'local structure alone cannot fully explain performance' but provides no satisfactory explanation

Reasoning graph construction has arbitrary choices: K=2000 clusters not justified, joint clustering across models creates dependencies, sentence segmentation heuristics ad-hoc, no validation that reconstructed graphs reflect actual reasoning steps

Limited scope and generalization: only mathematical reasoning tested; all models trained primarily on math; findings may not generalize to other reasoning domains (coding, logical reasoning, commonsense)
Statistical rigor issues: no error bars or confidence intervals; no significance testing; high variance in box plots not adequately discussed; similarity threshold for clustering appears arbitrary
No explanation for counterintuitive findings: why does RL compress correct trajectories while Base models don't? Why should steeper decay rates improve Pass@1?
Missing sensitivity analyses in main paper: K selection, embedding model choice, segmentation strategy all lack thorough ablation; key design validations relegated to appendix
No baseline comparisons: no comparison with random/null graph structures (Erdos-Renyi, scale-free models) to contextualize observed patterns; no shuffled control
Limited practical impact: doesn't lead to new training methods or actionable insights for practitioners; helps explain known phenomena but doesn't advance understanding

strengths: Novel analytical framework examining RL vs SFT at trajectory and step levels with creative reasoning graph construction and exponential decay analysis
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple model sizes (1.5B-14B), datasets (AIME, AMC, HumanEval), and model families (Qwen, DeepSeek, Nemotron, Llama)
Thorough ablation studies and robustness checks demonstrating methodological rigor (varying K, distance metrics, embeddings, similarity thresholds)
Clear and intuitive presentation with compelling 'squeeze' vs 'expand' framing that explains why SFT+RL training is effective
Extensive supplementary material with implementation details, additional results, and representative examples supporting reproducibility
Practical relevance with potential implications for training recipe design and data curation
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core findings (RL compresses solutions, SFT teaches new strategies) align with existing Pass@k literature; main contribution is quantification rather than new insights

Methodological concerns with reasoning graph construction: arbitrary design choices (K=2000, threshold=60) lack principled justification, conversion from continuous to discrete space causes information loss, not mechanistic but post-hoc interpretation

Weak causal claims: reasoning graphs constructed after inference, unclear whether observed properties are causes or consequences of performance; correlations shown but not conclusive evidence of causation

Limited theoretical grounding: unclear why exponential decay should appear, why steeper decay is better, or why graph properties should matter for reasoning; connections largely assumed rather than explained

Experimental design limitations: different models use different RL methods and checkpoints, SFT models are distillations from DeepSeek-R1 creating confounds, response length differences (Figure 13) could affect analyses, no controlled comparisons with identical training except RL vs SFT
Scope limitations: only tested on verifiable domains (math, code), only RLVR approach, results may not generalize to open-ended reasoning or other RL variants
Incomplete theoretical engagement: limited discussion of how findings relate to prior Pass@k analysis; missing mechanistic or theoretical justification for key observations
Statistical rigor issues: limited confidence intervals and error bars in main figures, no significance testing for observed differences, unclear sample sizes for some analyses
Reproducibility concerns: code link redacted, reliance on specific model checkpoints, some hyperparameter choices lack justification or sensitivity analysis in main text
